author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read the nginx error log. It goes to the data collector by syslog, from nginx itself or through the host's syslog daemon. Lines about a request go to HTTP, failed HTTP basic authentication to Auth, and lines with no request stay in generic.
notes:
Setup:
- Send the error log with error_log syslog:server=<collector> <level>; (tag nginx, facility local7), or forward the error log file through the host's syslog daemon.

Field mapping:
- Lines about a request go to HTTP: the client address, the Host header (else the server name), the referrer, method, path and query, with the error text, level, server name, upstream and connection number in event_metadata.
- access forbidden by rule, limiting requests and limiting connections mark the request blocked; their dry runs and delayed requests don't.
- Failed HTTP basic authentication (user "<name>": password mismatch, or user "<name>" was not found in "<file>") goes to Auth as a failed logon with the user, the client address and the site; nginx logs no line for a sign-in that worked.
- Lines with no request, such as TLS handshake failures and process or configuration messages, stay in generic.
- Messages are free text, so a message these parsers don't name still goes to HTTP when it has a request, with its text in event_metadata.

Time:
- The error log's time has no zone, so it is read as UTC unless an RFC 5424 header from a forwarder gives one.

Sources and licenses:
- nginx documents the levels and the syslog target but not the line, so these parsers follow nginx's source: ngx_log.c writes the time, [level], pid#tid and *connection, ngx_syslog.c the syslog header, and the HTTP error handler in ngx_http_request.c adds client, server, request, subrequest, upstream, host and referrer after the message.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up from the message formats in nginx's source (the access, auth_basic, limit_req and limit_conn modules).

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16 (105 of 105 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (99 of 99 fields, each line taken in 5 of 5 runs).
- No built-in parser claimed these lines.
